newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian railmen threaten wider strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian railmen threaten wider strike.

text.p: Striking Croatian railway workers threatened on Sunday to bring all rail traffic in the country to a standstill unless the government stopped intimidating them, state news agency HINA reported.

Some 11,000 workers of the loss-making Croatian state railways (HZ) halted nearly 80 percent of services demanding higher wages and better working conditions. International services and some cargo trains continued to operate.
The HZ management earlier threatened to sack workers who ignored its demand to go back to work.
Zlatko Pavletic,the head of the railway workers' union, said on Sunday the remaining skeleton services would be suspended if government pressure on strikers continued, HINA said.
"Such intimidations are illegal and they are aimed at fooling the public," Pavletic said.
He said the HZ was asking workers to fill in forms specifying their working hours during the strike.
But the government on Sunday stood firm by its refusal to negotiate on the workers' demands, saying they had no basis.
HZ said it was suffering daily losses of some 1.6 million kuna ($300,000) from the strike, and it was unable to guarantee that workers would get their November salaries.

"The railway workers' union will have to bear responsibility if we fail to pay November wages, since by organising the strike it prevented Croatian railmen from earning their money," HINA quoted a HZ statement as saying.
